identity.title: Evidence for the Disruption of a Planetary System During the Formation of the Helix Nebula

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we combine infrared (SOFIA, *Spitzer*, *Herschel*) and millimetre (ALMA) observations of the system to determine the origin of this excess using multi-wavelength imaging and radiative transfer modelling.
The ALMA millimetre-wavelength observations are likewise non-detections in both continuum and line emission.

question.value: What is the origin of the infrared excess around the Helix Nebula central white dwarf WD 2226-210: a remnant planetesimal belt, a cometary cloud, or a post-AGB disc?

evidence.quote: In this article we focus our efforts on deducing the origin and nature of the unresolved excess emission observed around the central white dwarf of the Helix Nebula.
It could be a remnant planetesimal belt, a cloud of comets, or the remnants of material shed during the post-asymptotic giant branch phase.
ALMA Band 6 observations of WD 2226-210 were obtained in Cycle 3 (PID: 2015.1.00762.S, PI: S. Ertel) and Cycle 4 (PID: 2016.1.00608.S, PI: S. Ertel).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data sets: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00762.S and #2016.1.00608.S.
In summary, we have obtained new images of the central regions of the Helix Nebula centred on the white dwarf with SOFIA/HAWC+ at 53 $\mu$m and ALMA in Band 6 ($\simeq1\,300~\mu$m).

claims.hypothesis: The excess arises from a remnant post-AGB circumbinary disc

evidence.quote: The non-detection of CO or SiO line emission from the white dwarf rules out the presence of substantial gas mass, contrary to expectations if the excess emission originated from a remnant post-AGB disc.
